# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 13 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 34 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_013_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 13

**1** Jesus said to his disciples: "Compare [тнт] me to something [лаау] and tell me what I am like [еіне]."

**2** Simon Peter said to him: "You are like a just [дікаіос] messenger [аggелос]."

**3** Matthew [матθаіос] said to him: "You are like a wise [сове] philosopher [чілосочос]."

**4** Thomas said to him: "Teacher [сав], my mouth is utterly unable [нечнатшом] to say [жоос] what you are like [еіне]."

**5** Jesus said: "I am not your teacher [сав]. Since you have drunk [со], you have become drunk [тохе] from the bubbling spring [пнге нмоу еттило] that I have tended [аре]."

**6** And he took him and withdrew [вок нсоун] and told him three [шомт] words [шаже].

**7** When Thomas returned [вок нсоун] to his companions [швер], they asked him: "What did Jesus say to you?"

**8** Thomas said to them: "If I tell you one of the words he told me, you will pick up stones and throw them at me, and fire will come from the stones and burn you up."

---

**Textual Notes (EMET):**
- *тнт*: to compare, liken; the disciples are to perform a comparison
- *аggелос*: Greek loan-word, "messenger/angel" — Peter's comparison preserves ambiguity
- *чілосочос*: Greek loan-word, "philosopher" — Matthew's comparison
- *сав*: master, teacher, rabbi — Thomas refuses to use this title for Jesus
- *пнге нмоу еттило*: "the bubbling/boiling spring of water"; Jesus is the source, Thomas has drunk from him
- *шомт шаже*: "three words" — what these three words are remains the great secret of the Gospel of Thomas
- The threat of stoning and fire reflects extreme esoteric content — the words are dangerous
- cf. Matt 16:13-20 (Peter's confession) — structurally parallel but Thomas, not Peter, receives the private revelation
